summary: Contrastive RAG at temp 1.2 (upper decoding endpoint)
hypothesis: Raising temperature to 1.2 on the best contrastive-RAG base should surface sharper, task-specific tail questions that greedy/default decoding misses — because the critical unknowns are hypothesised to live in the tail of the distribution.
technique: The exp011 contrastive-RAG pipeline (good-vs-bad exemplar retrieval injected as few-shot context) is run with decoding temperature raised to 1.2 — the upper endpoint of the decoding lever — to sample deeper into the tail and test whether coverage-filling questions can be surfaced that way.
